newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese bonds end buoyed after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bonds end buoyed after U.S. data.

text.p: 1707 GMT - Portuguese longer bonds ended buoyed after U.S. Producer Prices data which were positive for markets in general. *March 97 futures up 0.19 points to 109.00 *Feb 06 cash 119.53 (119.40), yld 6.56 vs 6.58 cls *Spread vs Spanish 10-yr cash -7 bps vs 0 bps cls

Portuguese longer bonds ended well-supported after favourable U.S. producer prices data but shorter bonds fell on the results of today's bond auction and fears over a rise in January prices, dealers said.
Dealers expected trade on Monday to be cautious ahead of the release of the January inflation data.

Shorter bonds lost ground after the Institute of Public Credit Management rejected bids at its three-year bond sale, with the weakness of the Spanish market also contributing to the decline, traders said.
Dealers said spreads against 10-year Bonos will stay negative.
The escudo recovered against the mark, benefiting from commercial operations, and stayed in tune with the peseta, dealers said. It stood at 100.46/49 per mark at 1720 GMT.
